Short answer: No — for tax year 2024 a typical W‑2 employee who is not self‑employed generally cannot claim a federal home‑office deduction because the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act suspended miscellaneous unreimbursed employee business expense deductions for tax years 2018–2025.  
There are narrow statutory exceptions (for example, certain qualified performing artists, some reservists, and fee‑basis public officials) and different treatment for statutory employees or taxpayers with self‑employment income, but those exceptions are narrowly defined and usually do not cover an ordinary salaried employee.  
The relevant authorities are the home‑office rules in IRC §280A (exclusive/regular use and principal place of business tests) together with the TCJA suspension of miscellaneous employee business expense deductions (P.L. 115‑97); if you were self‑employed, §280A and Schedule C rules would govern the deduction.  
Your records (square footage, direct and indirect costs, employer’s written requirement) are the right kind of substantiation if an exception applies, but the employer’s written mandate alone does not override the statutory suspension for ordinary employees.  
If you think a narrow exception or a different filing status might apply to your facts, you may wish to consult a tax advisor to review the statutes and factual tests before filing.
